profiles.name: squid-follow
profiles.notes: Broad dorsal red variation remains subtle, with smooth highlights and unchanged habitat framing.
independentNotes: Viewed baseline/current DOM and native GL. The dorsal red mantle now carries soft broad darker patches, with the original fins, arms and body silhouette remaining clear.
The added variation is coherent rather than visibly speckled in these stills. Sand caustics, vegetation, rocks, prey and the follow framing retain their clarity.

profiles.name: squid-phone
profiles.notes: Low-quality phone shading retains a clear squid silhouette without visible fine-grain aliasing.
independentNotes: Viewed all four low-quality phone images. Broad pigment variation remains visible at the smaller scale without additional visible grain or loss of the red mantle silhouette.

The environment and existing controls retain their framing. The lower fin reaches the existing control dock in both baseline and current DOM views; this is a retained limitation rather than a new regression.

profiles.notes: All five anatomy labels remain separated on the side rails, including the formerly overlapping Fin and Mantle.
independentNotes: Viewed all four desktop inspection images. All five current anatomy labels are readable and separated on the two side rails, including the formerly adjacent Fin and Mantle labels.

Thin leaders identify the specimen without opaque labels covering its central mantle, eye or arms. Native GL shows the same specimen framing and environment with restrained dorsal variation and a preserved pale underside.

profiles.name: nautilus-phone-inspection
profiles.notes: Shell, Eye and Tentacles callouts are separate and visible; the nautilus and environment remain visually unchanged.
independentNotes: Viewed all four nautilus phone inspection images. Shell, Eye and Tentacles are readable and separated; Tentacles is now visible where the baseline omits that callout.
The upright shell, head and tentacle fan stay within the frame. The native GL pair retains the same shell colors, skin texture and environment, with callout boxes outside the central shell and head.

history: The initial isolated-fork CPU batch collected only four of nine files and failed three protected snapshots at their former 20 or 30 second limits. Worker startup errors prevented five requested files from being collected. Its passing outcomes are retained as history and do not count toward final validation.

An isolated-thread diagnostic passed the six squid surface cases but failed to start the label worker. A single reusable thread then passed the full 128-case collection. Only the four expensive protected snapshot time budgets changed to 240 seconds; their sampling and assertions stayed intact.

The initial native batch passed three species callout cases. Its squid landscape case exposed a genuinely short inspection stage, fixed by reserving measured title, label and toolbar height and recalculating on entry and exit. Two squid shader cases could not mount because the root test wrapper supplied an absolute source path to the relative-URL harness; the wrapper now uses the canonical relative source.

The final CPU and native batches are separately bound to the final source and current test hashes. Automatic retries are disabled. Copied-source mutation checks contribute no extra ordinary CPU cases. Raw diagnostic logs, reports and initial failure screenshots remain local ignored evidence.
limits: Chromium DPR1 software WebGL; no hardware FPS, physical-phone or WebKit claim.
The bounded broad mottle is an illustrative squid pigment finish. Geometry and animation are protected; no performance improvement is claimed.
The native inspection controls may hide intervening rocks. The capture helper changes neither actors nor camera independently of those controls.
Raw runner logs, failure artifacts and frozen source snapshots remain local ignored evidence. Curated reversal data reconstructs only the exact matching baseline.
